penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: A genuine CWV performance audit and fix-prioritization report for a specific Magento site requires site-specific analysis, code-level investigation, and prioritized recommendations — per-customer work that cannot be fully automated to production quality for paying clients.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Magento agencies and developers will ask follow-up questions about specific fixes, implementation guidance, and re-testing — requiring ongoing human judgment.

rationale: Magento agencies and e-commerce digital teams are legitimate B2B buyers with real budget (they pay $100–500+/month for SEO tooling), and the lab-vs-field CWV gap is a documented, revenue-linked pain. However, the actionable deliverable — telling a specific site owner WHY their INP or LCP is failing in field data and WHAT to fix — requires site-specific RUM data instrumentation and per-site code analysis. This cannot run autonomously at the required quality level; each engagement is effectively a performance consulting project. The penalties for per-customer fulfillment and support drop this below validate.
solution_plan: Not recommended for build in current form. The idea would be a Magento-specific CWV monitoring + fix-prioritization micro-service. The buildability challenge: meaningful field data (RUM) requires a JavaScript snippet installed on the client's site, and the resulting diagnostics require per-site interpretation. A Claude-generated generic audit report would not be differentiated enough for agencies who already know the basics. Without a proprietary RUM data layer, this is either a thin commodity or a consulting engagement — neither suits the autonomous factory model.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy (4 < floor of 7) and buildability_with_ai (5 < floor of 6). The core deliverable is inherently per-site manual work. Drop.
